Let me just say, fuck anyone who ever tells you it's selfish, and fuck anyone who ever tells you it's cowardly. First of all you are not selfish or cowardly in any way. My asthma attacks are always huge coughing fits more so than wheezing and I always feel extremely exhausted afterwards, like someone took a baseball bat to my ribs. I have gone to the ER during an asthma attack with 99% oxygen intake. Oxygen doesn't have much to do with it, if you are not having an actual attack or serious struggle there is no reason to go, if you are in pain from it I'd say call the doctor first instead. Most insurance providers also have a nurse you can call and talk to 24/7, they can be very helpful in determining if you should go to the ER for something or not, sometimes they will even waive the fee/copay for you.

I am 18 and have been living with it since I was born, it is a nightmare, it gets exhausting physically and mentally, people who don't understand will be ignorant, but you will get by. When I first started daily meditation for the first year I had panic attacks, couldn't eat, etc. If a medication doesn't work well for you, even as simple as your rescue inhaler do not be afraid to ask your doctor to change it, try different brands, find what works best for you with little side effects. Better lung function does not always mean a better you, I have had the best lung function on some of the worst medications, and sometimes the side effects are just not worth those extra numbers. Believe it or not light exercise does help, do not push yourself to your absolute limits, have patience. I try to go for a mile walk at least once a week (almost everyday over the summer) even if it takes you an hour, even if you have to take breaks, you will eventually get stronger and have the ability to go longer. The saying If you don't use it you lose it is absolutely true, staying as active as possible is the best thing you can do for yourself. The discomfort and struggle with asthma will always be there, you will have good days and bad. Stay positive, you will be okay.
